subject: Support response SLAs & temporary exception request for P1/P2 coverage (us-east-1)
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@solsticehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency incident + support SLA question

Hannah / Marissa,

We had a production spike for our Solstice Health integration this morning in us-east-1; tail latency spiked above 2.5s for a sustained 25-minute window and some of our background jobs timed out. Our on-call saw retries and some customers reported slow UI load.

We need to clarify what Redwood's committed response times are for P1 and P2 incidents and whether you can provide an exception (temporary elevated coverage) while we complete our migration to the dedicated pool next week. Specifically:
- Can P1 incidents get an acknowledgement within 1 hour and a mitigation ETA within 2 hours?
- Can P2 be acknowledged within 4 hours?
- Is weekend/late-night on-call coverage guaranteed for production-impacting incidents?

Please see attached incident-summary-0502.pdf (ops timeline + traces). We need to know if Redwood is willing to sign a 30-day amendment that guarantees faster response while we stabilize. If an exception is possible, what is the escalation path (names/phones) and what commercial terms apply (credits/fees)?

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Platform Ops
Solstice Health
ops@solsticehealth.com


From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency incident + support SLA question

Anita — thanks for the heads up and for the attach. I reviewed the traces briefly; we saw increased queuing on a subset of endpoints feeding into your pool. We own this with high priority.

Quick summary of what we can do now and the next steps:
1) Temporary support exception (proposal):
   - P1 (sev 1, production down or customer-facing outage): acknowledgement within 1 hour, active mitigation ETA within 2 hours.
   - P2 (degraded but not down): acknowledgement within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 8 hours.
2) On-call coverage: 24x7 on-call engineer rotation; if event is P1 during nights/weekends we escalate to on-call manager within 30 minutes of detection.
3) Escalation path (proposed): on-call engineer -> Marissa Cole (on-call manager) -> Markus Klein (VP Eng) -> Customer Success Director (for commercial escalations).
4) Commercial: we can do a 30-day amendment; typical approach is limited credit cap for SLA misses tied to severity and duration. Need sales approval for specific credit cap.

I'll loop in Jordan and Marissa to confirm commercial language and have a formal amendment drafted. If you can confirm the mitigation targets above in writing, we'll prepare the DocuSign and an internal on-call roster for your account.

I will also open an internal incident ticket and tag your trace IDs.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency incident + support SLA question

Hannah/Jordan — flagged. A couple points from CS/ops perspective:
- We can support the proposed 1-hour/4-hour ack windows as a temporary exception for up to 30 days provided we get:
  * Signed amendment (I attached SLA-amendment-draft-0502.pdf)
  * Explicit credit cap and rollback criteria (recommend: credits capped at 5% total monthly invoice for the exception window)
  * On-call roster (oncall-rotation-2026.csv attached) and emergency phone number.
- Risk: if this becomes a recurring pattern outside the dedicated pool migration, we'll need to move to a higher commit level (dedicated capacity or higher-tier SLA).
- Operational ask: we need Solstice to log all incidents in the HubSpot ticket (link below) and allow our on-call access to the traces for faster triage.

I recommend we AUTO-APPROVE the technical exception pending Jordan's commercial sign-off and legal review of the amendment. Jordan — can you confirm credits/contract changes and loop in legal? Rafael — please prep a short customer note that we can send once legal gives greenlight.

—Marissa
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 May 2026 15:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency incident + support SLA question

Team — I spoke briefly to Solstice procurement and they're amenable to a 30-day exception while the migration completes. Commercial terms I can approve:
- 30-day amendment with the ack windows Hannah proposed.
- Credit cap: up to 5% of monthly bill for the amendment period; any credit beyond that requires Director-level approval.
- No change to base pricing; this is a temporary operational commitment only.

Requests before we send to the customer:
- Legal to review amendment language (Rita in Legal, cc'd manually once we send).
- VP Eng sign-off on escalation/responsibility (Markus, please confirm you'll accept escalation for P1 outside normal hours).

If Markus confirms, I'll generate the DocuSign envelope and Rafael can send the customer-facing note. Deal: RDW-9812 (HubSpot link included).

—Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita.rao@solsticehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 May 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Agreed temporary SLA amendment and next steps (DocuSign sent)

Anita — thanks for the quick sync. Per our internal approvals, here's the agreed plan and next steps:

Agreed temporary commitments (30 days starting on DocuSign signature):
- P1: acknowledgement within 1 hour, active mitigation ETA within 2 hours.
- P2: acknowledgement within 4 hours, mitigation plan within 8 hours.
- 24x7 on-call rotation; P1 escalates to Marissa (on-call manager) within 30 minutes, then to Markus (VP Eng) if unresolved after 60 minutes from manager escalation.
- Commercial: credit cap 5% for the amendment window.

Required from Solstice:
- Sign the amendment sent via DocuSign (link: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/abcde-12345).
- Log incidents in the HubSpot ticket and grant our on-call access to traces.

Attachments sent: SLA-amendment-draft-0502.pdf, oncall-rotation-2026.csv. We also attached a redlined incident summary for transparency (incident-summary-0502.pdf).

Once we have the signed DocuSign, Marissa's team will publish the on-call roster and Jordan will update the billing commit for the month. Rafael will send the customer-facing confirmation note.

If you are comfortable with these terms, please sign the DocuSign envelope and reply to confirm. We'll treat the signing date as the amendment effective date.

—Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
